## Findings
- claim-1: The lower-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) generates \(J_v\); the cited theorem proves its minimality. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]
- claim-2: For every valid \((n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\), no nonzero homogeneous syzygy of the lower-adjoined form exists. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 270-304]
- claim-3: Let \(q=n-r\), \(p=q-i\), \(c=r-j\), and \[ v^\vee=v_{q,\;q+j-i,\;q-i+1,\;n}. \] Then \(v^\vee\) is bigrassmannian, its parameters are \[ (i^\vee,j^\vee,a^\vee,b^\vee)=(j,i,a,b), \] and \[ J_v/A_+J_v\cong \bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})} \mathbb Z[\bar s_\mu]. \] Hence \(G_R\) is an integral homogeneous basis of indecomposables, is an irredundant generating family of \(J_v\), and \[ \operatorname{Hilb}_{J_v/A_+J_v}(z) =z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z. \]
## Strategy
Let \(q=n-r\), \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), and \(A_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}A_d\). For a bigrassmannian \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), set
\[
i=s-t+1,\quad j=r-t+1,\quad
a=\min(q-i,r-j),\quad b=\min(i,j).
\]
The source supplies lower-adjoined generation and its no-syzygy input [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235; 819-831]. Use the accepted lower-adjoined integral-basis certificate and accepted quotient-conjugation certificate.

Define
\[
v^\vee=v_{q,\ q+j-i,\ q-i+1,\ n}.
\]
Then
\[
(i^\vee,j^\vee,a^\vee,b^\vee)=(j,i,a,b).
\]
Indeed \(t^\vee=q-i+1\) and \(s^\vee=q+j-i\), so
\[
1\le t^\vee\le q,\qquad t^\vee\le s^\vee\le n,\qquad
t^\vee>q+s^\vee-n.
\]
The transformed validity inequalities are explicitly
\[
a+j^\vee=a+i\le q=r^\vee,\qquad
a+i^\vee=a+j\le r=n-r^\vee,\qquad
b\le i^\vee,j^\vee.
\]

Let \(A^\vee=\Lambda/I_{q,r}\). Partition conjugation gives the accepted graded integral isomorphism
\[
\Omega_Q:\ J_v/A_+J_v\xrightarrow{\sim}
J_{v^\vee}/A^\vee_+J_{v^\vee},
\qquad [\bar s_\lambda]\longmapsto[\bar s_{\lambda'}].
\]
The lower basis for \(v^\vee\) is indexed by
\[
\nu=(j^i,\rho),\qquad \rho\subseteq b^a.
\]
Writing \(\alpha=\rho'\subseteq a^b\),
\[
(j^i,\rho)'=
(i+\alpha_1,\ldots,i+\alpha_b,i^{\,j-b}).
\]
Hence its inverse-conjugate is exactly
\[
G_R=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}.
\]
Therefore the residue classes of \(G_R\) form a homogeneous integral basis
\[
J_v/A_+J_v\cong
\bigoplus_{\mu\in G_R}\mathbb Z[\bar s_\mu].
\]

For generation, let \(M=A\,G_R\). Since the residue classes span the quotient,
\[
J_v=M+A_+J_v.
\]
As \(A\) is finite graded, \(A_+\) is nilpotent. Iterating gives
\[
J_v=M+A_+^kJ_v=M
\]
for \(k\gg0\). Thus \(G_R\) generates \(J_v\). Removing any member would make the remaining residue classes span the quotient, contradicting their basis property; hence this generation is irredundant.

Finally \(|\mu|=ij+|\alpha|\), with \(\alpha\subseteq a^b\). Thus
\[
\operatorname{Hilb}_{J_v/A_+J_v}(z)
=z^{ij}\sum_{\alpha\subseteq a^b}z^{|\alpha|}
=z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z.
\]

The requested standalone right-adjoined indecomposables theorem is established, conditional only on the stipulated accepted admissibility, lower-basis, and quotient-conjugation certificates.

## Gaps
No gap remains under those accepted certificates. Without quotient-conjugation, the source itself only remarks that a transposed proof could be made; it does not state this integral indecomposables theorem.
